Welcome to the registration page for the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2026), taking place October 24–29, 2026, in Budapest, Hungary.

Whether attending in person or virtually, this page provides information on registration categories, pricing, paper presentation registration, deadlines, and conference policies.

Please note: Conference Registration and Paper Presentation Registration are separate requirements. (Paper registrations occur within the conference registration and is not a separate registration)

## Accepted Paper Information

All individuals participating in EMNLP 2026 must complete either an In-Person Conference Registration or a Virtual Conference Registration.

Conference Registration and Paper Presentation Registration are separate requirements. (Paper registrations occur within the conference registration and is not a separate registration)

## Paper Presentation Registration Requirements

All accepted Main Conference, Findings, Computational Linguistics (CL), Transactions of the ACL (TACL), Industry Track, Demo, and Workshop papers must be registered, and the applicable Paper Presentation Registration Fee paid by the applicable Paper Registration Deadline to remain in the conference program and proceedings.

## Exceptions

Accepted Findings papers that are not being presented are not required to pay the Paper Presentation Registration Fee and will remain in the proceedings. Authors attending the conference must still complete a conference registration.

Shared Task Workshop papers are not required to pay the Paper Presentation Registration Fee. However, any author or designated presenter attending the conference must complete a conference registration.

| 3–4 Papers | $200 |
| 5–6 Papers | $300 |

A single qualifying conference registration may register a maximum of six (6) accepted papers.

| Paper Type | Paper Registration Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| Main Conference papers | September 11, 2026 |
| Workshop papers | September 24, 2026 |

The presenting author or designated presenter may complete their personal conference registration after the applicable Paper Registration Deadline, provided the paper has already been registered using a qualifying conference registration.

Papers that are not registered by the applicable Paper Registration Deadline will be removed from the conference program and proceedings.

## ACL Membership

All conference attendees must have a current 2026 ACL Membership.

If you do not already have a current ACL Membership, the appropriate membership will be added during registration.

## Registration Policies

By registering for EMNLP 2026, attendees agree to comply with all applicable conference policies, including:

Cancellation, Attendance Format Changes & Refund Policy Badge Use & Reprint Policy Paper Presentation Registration Requirements ACL Code of Ethics ACL Anti-Harassment Policy Accessibility Assistance Privacy Policy Photography & Recording Notice

## Cancellation, Attendance Format Changes & Refund Policy

The Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL) is committed to supporting our attendees while ensuring fairness and predictability in managing event registrations. Please review our Cancellation, Change & Refund Policy carefully before completing your registration.

### Change Fees

A US$25 administrative change fee applies to the following registration changes:

- Switching from in-person to virtual
- Switching from virtual to in-person (if capacity allows)

After October 8, 2026, presentation formats are final and no additional presentation changes will be permitted.

If your visa has not yet been approved, ACL recommends registering as a Virtual Presenter. Once your visa is approved, you may request a change to In-Person Presentation, subject to conference deadlines and scheduling availability.

### Cancellation Deadlines & Fees

On or Before September 24

- Full refund less US $50 processing fee

September 25 – October 1

- Cancellation permitted
- US $200 cancellation fee
- OR convert to Virtual Attendance at no additional charge

October 2 – October 8

- No cancellation refunds
- May convert to Virtual Registration changes are permitted only between equivalent registration types. Registrants may not downgrade from one registration product to another after purchase. Refunds will be calculated using the equivalent registration category only. Registrations may not be converted to a different registration product or package.

After October 8

- No refunds
- No presentation changes

Exceptions

All exceptions must be submitted in writing with supporting documentation for review and approval by ACL.

Visa Denials: If a visa application is denied, registrants may convert their registration to Virtual Attendance. Registration changes are permitted only between equivalent registration types. Registrants may not downgrade from one registration product to another after purchase. Refunds will be calculated using the equivalent registration category only. Registrations may not be converted to a different registration product or package.

For example:

Permitted ✔ Full Conference In-Person → Full Conference Virtual ✔ Tutorial & Workshop Only In-Person → Tutorial & Workshop Only Virtual

Not Permitted ✘ Full Conference In-Person → Tutorial Only Virtual ✘ Full Conference In-Person → One-Day Workshop ✘ Two-Day Workshop → One-Day Workshop ✘ Conference Registration → Tutorial Registration

LINGUIST List 37.972 Confs: 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (Hungary)

### LINGUIST List 37.972

#### Tue Mar 10 2026

#### Confs: 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (Hungary)

Editor for this issue: Valeriia Vyshnevetska <valeriialinguistlist.org>

---

---

2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language ProcessingShort Title: EMNLP

Date: 24-Oct-2026 - 29-Oct-2026Location: Budapest, HungaryMeeting URL: https://2026.emnlp.org/

Linguistic Field(s): Computational Linguistics

Submission Deadline: 25-May-2026

EMNLP 2026 invites the submission of long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research on empirical methods for Natural Language Processing. EMNLP 2026 has a goal of curating a diverse technical program—in addition to traditional research results, papers may contribute negative findings, survey an area, announce the creation of a new resource, argue a position, report novel linguistic insights derived using existing computational techniques, and reproduce (or fail to reproduce) previous results. As in recent years, some of the presentations at the conference will be of papers accepted by the Transactions of the ACL (TACL) and the Computational Linguistics (CL) journals.

Important Dates: - ARR submission deadline (long & short papers) May 25, 2026 - Reviewer registration deadline for ALL authors May 27, 2026 - Author response and author-reviewer discussion July 7 - July 13, 2026 - Meta review released July 30, 2026 - EMNLP commitment deadline August 2, 2026 - Notification of acceptance (long & short papers) August 20, 2026 - Camera-ready papers due (long & short) September 20, 2026 - Main Conference (dates for Workshops/Tutorials TBD) October 22 - 26, 2026Note: All deadlines are 11:59PM UTC-12:00 (“anywhere on Earth”).

Following the ACL and ARR policies, there is no anonymity period requirement.

At the time of submission to ARR, authors will be asked to select a preferred venue (e.g., EMNLP 2026). This is used only to calculate acceptance rates. Authors who selected EMNLP 2026 as a preferred venue when submitting to ARR may choose not to commit to EMNLP 2026 after receiving their reviews, and authors who selected a preferred venue other than EMNLP 2026 when submitting to ARR are still welcome to commit to EMNLP 2026.

New: Paper Integrity Policies at EMNLP

There is growing concern in our community regarding unethical paper submissions that overwhelm community resources, including but not limited to, thinly sliced contributions, submissions with hallucinated citations, and entirely AI-generated papers (AI writing assistance is permitted). EMNLP will take actions against such submissions, as well as submissions that violate the ACL Policy on Publication Ethics. Such submissions may be desk rejected, and all authors involved in the submission may be ineligible to commit their paper(s) to EMNLP 2026 and EMNLP 2027.

Paper Submission Information:

Dual submissions are not allowed! Please check the ARR Multiple Submission Policy for details. Papers must be submitted, at latest, by the ARR 2026 May cycle. Papers that have received reviews and a meta-review from ARR (whether from the ARR 2026 May cycle or an earlier ARR cycle) may be committed to EMNLP via the commitment link.

Mandatory Reviewing Workload:

All authors are expected to sign up to review, or serve as an Area Chair or Senior Area Chair, with assignments subsequently based on qualifications. After submission, all authors must complete the author registration form by May 27, 2026 EoD AoE. If you receive assignments, your reviews must be completed by July 6, or your meta-reviews - by July 29. In case of any emergencies, the chairs should be warned via the emergency declaration form.

Highly irresponsible reviewers may be ineligible to (re-)submit or commit their work during the next ARR cycle. The submitting authors should (a) make sure that all other authors are aware of this policy, and (b) check that everybody on their team(s) submits their (meta-)reviews on time and in accordance with the guidelines. You can read additional details on the definition of highly irresponsible reviewers and the corresponding ARR policy here: https://aclrollingreview.org/incentives2025

AI Reviewing Experiment (opt-in):

The Program Committee plans on running an opt-in AI Reviewing Experiment to collect feedback from authors on the utility of AI Reviewers in the review process. The AI Reviews for opted-in submissions will not inform any part of the conference decision process. We will run this experiment under IRB approval, using open-weights models running on in-house compute resources, or closed models that guarantee zero-data retention.

Submission Topics:

EMNLP 2026 aims to have a broad technical program. Relevant topics for the conference include, but are not limited to, the following areas: - Clinical and Biomedical Applications - NLP and Code Models - Computational Social Science and Cultural Analytics - Dialogue and Interactive Systems - Discourse and Pragmatics - Efficient Methods for NLP - Ethics, Bias, and Fairness - NLP and Symbolic Reasoning - Generation - Human-Centered NLP and Human-AI Interaction - Information Extraction - Information Retrieval and Text Mining - Interpretability and Analysis of Models for NLP - Language Modeling - LLM Agents - LLM Security - Linguistic Theories, Cognitive Modeling, and Psycholinguistics - Machine Learning for NLP - Machine Translation - Multilingualism and Cross-Lingual NLP - Multimodality and Language Grounding to Vision, Robotics and Beyond - NLP Applications - Phonology, Morphology, and Word Segmentation - Question Answering - Resources and Evaluation - Semantics: Lexical and Sentence-Level - Sentiment Analysis, Stylistic Analysis, and Argument Mining - Speech Recognition, Text-to-Speech and Spoken Language Understanding - Summarization - Syntax: Tagging, Chunking and Parsing

Special Theme: New Missions for NLP Research

EMNLP 2026 Theme Track: New Missions for NLP Research Large language models have rapidly shifted from research prototypes to widely used infrastructure. This new reality is changing the center of gravity of NLP research, and progress can no longer be measured only by fractional improvements in benchmark scores. When strong general-purpose models are increasingly available through open releases and commercial platforms, the field faces a more foundational question: What are the missions of NLP research now, and what kinds of contributions most advance that mission?

The EMNLP 2026 special theme invites papers that articulate, test, and advance visions for NLP in this era. We welcome work that reflects on the mission(s) of NLP research, reframes our collective research goals, proposes new evaluation and scientific methodologies, and builds bridges across multiple disciplines that can sharpen both our theories and our impact. Submissions may be empirical, theoretical, or position and survey papers, but should be grounded in clear claims, strong evidence, and actionable insights.

Relevant topics include, but are not limited to:

- Rethinking progress and evaluation in NLPFor example, going beyond static leaderboards, including real-world impact, trustworthiness, robustness, and longitudinal behavior; what “generalization” should mean for humans vs models, and when models are reused, adapted, and deployed in diverse settings, etc.

- From models to systems and ecosystemsFor example, how does system-level research on agentic workflows, tool use, and multi-model orchestration interface with human experiences; and at an ecosystem level, how do people, organizations, and communities use and interact with language technology.

- Scientific understanding of language and cognitionFor example, using contemporary models as experimental instruments for psycholinguistics, cognitive science, language acquisition, and field linguistics; and what models reveal, and fail to reveal, about human cognition, the nature of language, learning, and meaning.

- Data as a bottleneck and a responsibilityFor example, research on data scarcity and limits, contamination, and the consequences of synthetic data feedback loops, and new approaches to data creation, documentation, governance, and consent.

- LLMs as research tools: AI in researchFor example, rigorous studies of how LLMs can support the research process in hypothesis generation, experiment design, analysis, and peer review support tools without eroding scientific standards.

This special theme is intended to complement the breadth of EMNLP, not narrow it. We encourage submissions that are ambitious in scope while remaining concrete in claims and methodology, and that help the community clarify what research looks like in the next chapter of NLP.

Two Stage Review:

Submission to ARR, Commitment to EMNLP:EMNLP 2026 will use ACL Rolling Review (ARR) as a reviewing system, but final decisions will be made by the conference. Both submissions of articles for review and commitment of reviewed articles to the conference will be performed via the Open Review platform. Specifically, authors will follow a two-step process:

1. Authors submit articles to ARR, where submissions receive reviews and meta-reviews from ARR reviewers and action editors; Authors commit their reviewed articles to a publication venue (e.g., EMNLP 2026), where Senior Area Chairs and Program Chairs make acceptance decisions from the ARR reviews and meta-reviews. Authorship during commitment. During the commitment phase, it is not allowed to modify the author list (i.e., addition/deletion of authors is not allowed). However, modification of author order is possible.

2. EMNLP 2026 has chosen this approach in coordination with *CL 2026 conferences, which are adopting the same procedure and a coordinated submission plan to allow maximum flexibility during their submission periods for the authors. At each cycle, after a paper has been fully reviewed, authors have the option to commit their paper to a conference, or revise and resubmit for another round of reviews.

The reviewing process will continue to be double-blind. Reviewers will not see authors, nor will authors see reviewers and reviews on ARR will not be made publicly visible. However, authors will be given the option through ARR to make their anonymized submitted articles publicly visible.

Paper Submission Detail:Both long and short paper submissions should follow all of the ARR submission requirements, including: - Long Papers (8 pages) and Short Papers (4 pages) - Instructions for Two-Way Anonymized Review - Authorship - Citation and Comparison - Multiple Submission Policy, Resubmission Policy, and Withdrawal Policy - ACL’s Publication Ethics Policy, and ARR’s Ethics Policy including the responsible NLP research checklist - ACL’s Disclosure Policy - Limitations - Writing Assistance - Paper Submission and Templates - Optional Supplementary Materials - Final versions of accepted papers will be given one additional page of content (up to 9 pages for long papers, up to 5 pages for short papers) to address reviewers’ comments.

Presentation at the Conference:

All accepted papers must be presented at the conference to appear in the proceedings. The conference will include both in-person and virtual presentation options. Papers without at least one presenting author registered by the early registration deadline may be subject to rejection. Long and short papers will be presented orally or as posters as determined by the program committee. While short papers will be distinguished from long papers in the proceedings, there will be no distinction in the proceedings between papers presented orally and papers presented as posters.

Contact Information:General Chair:André Martins, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa

Program Chairs:Sunipa Dev, GoogleDesmond Elliott, University of CopenhagenHung-yi Lee, National Taiwan UniversityJessy Li, The University of Texas at Austin

For questions related to paper submission, and the review process in general, email: [email protected]

For questions about commitment and post review related topics, email: [email protected]

results.title: EMNLP 2026: Dates, Deadlines, Venue & Program | zPlatform.ai
results.text:
EMNLP 2026: Dates, Deadlines, Venue & Program | zPlatform.ai

TL;DR: EMNLP 2026, the Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, runs October 24-29, 2026 at Hungexpo in Budapest, Hungary, organized by ACL’s SIGDAT. The program covers a main research track reviewed through ACL Rolling Review, an industry track built around real-world deployment problems, 30 accepted workshops, tutorials, and a demo track. As of this writing, the organizers have not published keynote speakers or registration pricing, so this guide sticks to what is actually confirmed.

Most conference guides do this backwards. They lead with a speaker list that turns out to be last year’s, or a ticket price pulled from a random aggregator instead of the organizer’s own page. I track AI and NLP conferences for the same reason I test AI tools with my own money: the research debated on these stages shows up in production systems a few months later.

EMNLP is not a vendor conference. It is a flagship venue for empirical NLP research, where the evaluation methodology in a paper you read here often ends up in the benchmark your team gets measured against next year, which matters more now that large language models have turned half the industry into amateur NLP researchers overnight.

In this guide, I will cover the confirmed dates and venue, what the submission tracks and special theme mean, who genuinely benefits from attending, what is known (and not known) about speakers and registration, and my honest verdict, checked directly against the official EMNLP 2026 site.

Short version: EMNLP 2026 is a research-first academic conference for people who build or study language technology, not a marketing event with a trade-show floor. If your team works on LLMs, evaluation, or applied NLP, it belongs on your calendar even with several details still marked “coming soon.”

## Key Takeaways

- Confirmed dates and venue, unconfirmed format. EMNLP 2026 runs October 24-29, 2026 at Hungexpo in Budapest, Hungary, but the official site does not yet state whether virtual or hybrid attendance will be offered.
- This is a research conference first. The program is built from ACL Rolling Review (ARR) submissions, not a curated keynote circuit.
- A dedicated deployment track exists. The industry track wants papers on latency, infrastructure, and human-in-the-loop systems, the problems academic papers usually skip.
- 30 workshops are already accepted, spanning legal NLP, multilingual representation learning, interpretability, climate NLP, speech and audio models, and more.
- Speakers and pricing are genuinely TBA. No keynote speakers are listed and the registration page reads “Coming soon,” so treat any third-party claim otherwise with suspicion.

A conference agenda full of workshop acronyms is not a weakness. It is the clearest sign that a research community has gotten specific enough to be useful.

## What Is EMNLP 2026?

EMNLP 2026 is the 2026 edition of one of the two or three most influential annual research conferences in NLP, organized by ACL’s SIGDAT, the Special Interest Group on Linguistic Data and Corpus-Based Approaches to Natural Language Processing. Unlike a practitioner conference, its core output is peer-reviewed research papers, not sponsored talks.

The main conference accepts long papers (8 pages) and short papers (4 pages), reviewed through ACL Rolling Review (ARR): a two-stage system where papers are reviewed and meta-reviewed on a rolling basis, then committed to a specific conference for a final decision. Authors committed to EMNLP 2026 through ARR by May 25, 2026, with acceptance notifications going out August 20, 2026.

The 2026 edition runs a special theme, “New Missions for NLP Research,” addressing what empirical NLP looks like once large language models are already deployed everywhere: evaluation methodology, using LLMs as research instruments rather than just subjects, and data governance.

One detail says a lot about where the field is headed. EMNLP 2026 is running an opt-in “AI Reviewing Experiment” alongside human review, explicitly stating AI-generated reviews “will not inform any part of the conference decision process,” right next to a Paper Integrity Policy banning entirely AI-generated papers, hallucinated citations, and thinly sliced submissions. That is a research community being honest about an unresolved tension, not a marketing talking point.

## When and Where Is EMNLP 2026?

EMNLP 2026 takes place October 24-29, 2026, at Hungexpo, Albertirsai út 10, 1101 Budapest, Hungary. The six-day window spans co-located tutorials and workshops on either end of the calendar alongside the main conference days, standard structure for an *ACL conference of this scale.

Budapest gives the conference a central European location, workable for attendees flying in from the UK, continental Europe, and the Middle East. Hungexpo is a large-scale exhibition venue built for high-attendance technical conferences, not a boutique hotel ballroom.

Here is the honest gap. The official site does not currently state whether EMNLP 2026 will offer virtual or hybrid attendance. Past editions have run hybrid formats, but nothing on the 2026 site confirms an online option yet. If remote attendance matters to your budget, that is the single biggest open question to track before committing to travel.

Quick facts:

| Detail | Information |
| --- | --- |
| Event | EMNLP 2026 (Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing) |
| Dates | October 24-29, 2026 |
| Venue | Hungexpo, Albertirsai út 10, 1101 Budapest, Hungary |
| Organizer | ACL’s SIGDAT |
| Format | In-person confirmed; virtual/hybrid attendance not yet confirmed |
| Review process | ACL Rolling Review (ARR), two-stage |
| Tracks | Main conference, industry track, tutorials, workshops (30 accepted), demos |
| Official site | 2026.emnlp.org |

## EMNLP 2026 Important Dates: The Full Deadline Timeline

If you searched “EMNLP 2026 timeline” or “important dates,” here is every deadline in one place, pulled straight from the official calls rather than a stale aggregator. The main conference runs on ACL Rolling Review (ARR), so the paper flow is submission first, then a separate binding commitment to EMNLP, then notification. All deadlines are 11:59pm AoE (UTC-12).

| Milestone (main conference, via ARR) | Date |
| --- | --- |
| ARR submission deadline (long & short papers) | May 25, 2026 |
| Reviewer registration deadline for all authors | May 27, 2026 |
| Author response & author-reviewer discussion | July 7-13, 2026 |
| Meta reviews released | July 30, 2026 |
| EMNLP commitment deadline | August 2, 2026 |
| Notification of acceptance | August 20, 2026 |
| Camera-ready papers due | August 30, 2026 |
| Main conference | October 24-29, 2026 |

One rule trips people up every cycle: for the ARR 2026 May cycle, which feeds both EMNLP and AACL, you must declare EMNLP 2026 as your target conference at submission time, and that choice is binding. Submit without selecting EMNLP and you cannot commit here later. See the official call for main conference papers for the exact policy.

### Industry, demo, and tutorial track deadlines

These three tracks do not use ARR and run their own OpenReview timelines, so the dates differ from the main conference:

- Industry track (no ARR, up to 6 pages, double-blind): submission June 16, rebuttal opens July 22, author response due July 29, notification August 20, camera-ready September 20.
- System demonstrations (single-blind, no rebuttal, live demo link required): submission July 10, notification August 20, camera-ready August 30.
- Tutorials: proposals were due June 1, with acceptance notified July 15.

Since today is well past most submission windows, the dates that still matter for authors are the August 2 commitment deadline, the August 20 notifications across every track, and the camera-ready cutoffs. If you were hunting for an “accepted papers list,” it does not exist yet: acceptances land August 20, and the full program plus the findings and workshop papers only get published in the ACL Anthology in the weeks after camera-ready. Anyone posting a definitive EMNLP 2026 accepted-papers list before then is guessing.

## Who Should Attend EMNLP 2026?

EMNLP 2026 is built for people who do or study NLP research, not general AI enthusiasts looking for a big-picture keynote. If you are weighing this against a broader AI business conference, it will feel narrow and technical unless you fit one of these profiles.

- NLP and LLM researchers, academic or industrial, presenting or reading peer-reviewed work on evaluation, language modeling, or the “New Missions” theme.
- Applied ML engineers working on language systems who care more about the industry track’s latency and deployment focus than leaderboard scores.
- Industry-track and demo-track presenters with a deployed system or practical case study, since the track explicitly welcomes vision papers grounded in deployment experience.
- Workshop-specific attendees working in legal NLP, climate NLP, multilingual representation learning, or interpretability, where the 30 workshops offer more depth than the main track alone.
- Early-career researchers and PhD students using the conference to network and benchmark their work.

Honest caveat: if your team wants vendor demos or a business-facing “AI strategy” overview, EMNLP is the wrong event. This is a peer-reviewed research conference, and much of its value assumes you already know the field’s vocabulary.

If you are an applied NLP engineer pitching EMNLP attendance to a manager who wants a business-facing AI conference with keynotes and vendor booths, it helps to frame the request narrowly. Say your actual need is specific, fighting evaluation drift on a clinical-note summarization model: the “New Missions” theme plus the industry track’s deployment focus map directly onto that. Requesting a smaller trip built around two specific sessions and the industry track, rather than the whole event, tends to get approved faster than a vague “let’s explore AI trends” pitch.

## Speakers and Program at EMNLP 2026

As of this writing, EMNLP 2026 has not published a keynote lineup, and no secondary source confirms one either. If you see a “confirmed speakers” list anywhere else, verify it against 2026.emnlp.org directly. I would rather say “not yet announced” than hand you a fabricated name.

What is confirmed is the program structure, and for a research conference that matters more than any single keynote. The main conference runs long and short paper sessions built entirely from ARR-reviewed submissions, while the industry track, tutorials, workshops, and demo track each run their own submission and review process, all converging on the same October 24-29 window. Papers accepted after the August 20 notification date will populate the official program in the following weeks. If you are deciding on travel now, commit based on the tracks and themes below rather than waiting on a speaker list that may land closer to the event.

## What Does the EMNLP 2026 Agenda Cover?

The agenda spans a main research track, an industry track, tutorials, 30 accepted workshops, and a demo track, each targeting a different slice of the NLP community.

The main conference covers language modeling, machine translation and multilingual NLP, information extraction, generation and summarization, dialogue systems, ethics and bias, interpretability, and multimodal work, plus the “New Missions” theme on evaluation methodology and LLMs as research instruments.

The industry track is where this event earns relevance for applied engineers, not just academics. Submissions max out at 6 pages, double-blind reviewed on OpenReview, covering system efficiency (latency, infrastructure, human-in-the-loop systems), novel applications built under real constraints, and methods for deployed systems (bias mitigation, evaluation, robustness).

Tutorials run in standard three-hour blocks, split between cutting-edge CL/NLP topics and introductory sessions on adjacent fields. The 30 accepted workshops span an unusually wide range, including MathNLP, ArabicNLP, Natural Legal Language Processing, BlackboxNLP (interpretability), Multilingual Representation Learning, ClimateNLP, BabyLM, Online Abuse and Harms (WOAH), Speech and Audio Language Models, FinNLP, and WMT.

If your team is evaluating language-model tooling alongside research like this, it is worth cross-checking against the broader agent ecosystem too, which I track separately on the best MCP servers leaderboard.

## EMNLP 2026 Registration and Pricing

Direct answer: EMNLP 2026 has not published registration pricing as of this writing. The official registration page currently reads “Coming soon,” with no fee schedule, early-bird window, student rate, or virtual-versus-in-person split listed anywhere.

I am not filling that gap with a guessed number or a discount code, since that is exactly what low-quality SEO content does before the facts exist. Past EMNLP editions have used tiered pricing (member versus non-member, student versus regular, in-person versus virtual), so expect something similar once the page updates, but treat any number quoted elsewhere right now as unverified. Bookmark the official registration page and check back, or subscribe for event alerts to get notified when verified pricing lands.

## Is EMNLP 2026 Worth It? My Honest Take

For NLP researchers and applied ML engineers working on language systems, EMNLP 2026 looks like one of the strongest research-first events on the 2026 calendar, precisely because it does not dumb itself down for a broader AI-hype audience. The industry track’s deployment focus, the “New Missions” theme’s honest reckoning with an LLM-saturated field, and 30 workshops deep enough to matter are real signals of substance.

The honest caveats are real too: no keynote speakers confirmed, no pricing yet, and an open question on virtual attendance. That is not a quality red flag, just where a research conference sits five months out, when submission deadlines still dominate the timeline over marketing copy. My buy-or-skip framing, the same one I apply to AI tool deals: commit to travel now only if you have a paper or submission tied to Budapest, or a specific track maps directly onto a problem your team is solving today. Wait if you are deciding purely on keynote lineup or price. Skip it if you need a business-facing AI strategy event rather than a peer-reviewed research conference.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### When and where is EMNLP 2026?

EMNLP 2026 runs October 24-29, 2026, at Hungexpo in Budapest, Hungary. In-person attendance is confirmed; virtual or hybrid attendance has not been confirmed on the official site.

### Who organizes EMNLP 2026?

EMNLP is organized by ACL’s SIGDAT, the Special Interest Group on Linguistic Data and Corpus-Based Approaches to Natural Language Processing.

### Are keynote speakers announced for EMNLP 2026?

No. The official site has not published a keynote lineup, and no reliable secondary source confirms one. Verify any speaker claims directly against 2026.emnlp.org.

### How much does EMNLP 2026 registration cost?

Pricing is not yet published. The registration page currently states “Coming soon,” with no fee schedule or discount code available.

### What is the EMNLP 2026 industry track?

A dedicated track for real-world deployment papers, covering system efficiency, novel applications, and methods for deployed systems. Submissions were capped at 6 pages and due June 16, 2026.

### How many workshops does EMNLP 2026 have?

30 workshops have been accepted, covering legal NLP, multilingual representation learning, interpretability, climate NLP, speech and audio models, and finance NLP.

## The Bottom Line

EMNLP 2026 is doing what a research conference should: leading with peer review, an honest special theme about NLP’s identity crisis in the LLM era, and a program built from 30 workshops and a deployment-focused industry track rather than a marketing keynote circuit.

The gaps in this guide, no confirmed speakers, no pricing, no confirmed virtual option, are the normal state of an academic conference five months out, not signs of disorganization. Anyone publishing a confident speaker list or discount code for EMNLP 2026 right now is guessing, not reporting. Your concrete next step: bookmark the official event site, watch the registration and program pages, and plan your trip around the tracks that map to your actual work. While you wait, browse how the field’s own tooling is evolving on the MCP server leaderboard.

## What Is EMNLP 2026?

The Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP) is a premier annual gathering for researchers and practitioners dedicated to the empirical study of language from a computational perspective. EMNLP 2026, scheduled for late October in Budapest, represents one of the most significant events in the AI calendar, specifically focused on the rapid advancements in natural language processing (NLP). The conference is organized under the auspices of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL) and its special interest group, SIGDAT, bringing together a global community that drives the field forward.

EMNLP has consistently served as the primary venue for presenting cutting-edge research that blends empirical methodology with theoretical insights in NLP, machine learning, and computational linguistics. The 2026 edition in Budapest will continue this tradition, providing a rigorous peer-reviewed forum for the latest discoveries. The conference’s reputation is built on its commitment to high-quality, reproducible research that often sets the agenda for the industry and academia for the year ahead, making EMNLP 2026 a critical checkpoint for the state of the art in language AI.

## Why It Matters for AI Professionals

For AI professionals, from researchers to engineers, EMNLP 2026 is more than just an academic conference; it is a direct line to the foundational shifts in language technology. The papers and presentations at EMNLP frequently introduce the novel architectures, training methodologies, and evaluation benchmarks that will underpin next-generation AI products and services. Attending provides an unparalleled opportunity to understand the limitations of current models and the emerging solutions that will address them, knowledge that is essential for strategic R&D planning.

Beyond the technical content, the event is a central hub for talent and collaboration. The discussions in hallways and during poster sessions often lead to new partnerships, hiring opportunities, and cross-pollination of ideas between industry labs and academic institutions. For professionals aiming to stay at the forefront of NLP, engaging with the EMNLP 2026 community is an invaluable investment in their technical currency and professional network.

## What to Expect

EMNLP 2026 will follow its established, comprehensive format designed to cater to various levels of expertise and interest. The week-long event typically begins with co-located workshops and tutorials, which offer deep dives into specialized topics and emerging sub-fields. These are followed by the main conference sessions, featuring oral presentations of peer-reviewed papers, keynote talks, and poster sessions where the bulk of the research is presented and discussed in detail.

While specific themes and speakers for EMNLP 2026 are yet to be announced, the conference consistently covers the core and evolving areas of the field. Attendees can expect a strong focus on:

- Large language model (LLM) efficiency, alignment, and evaluation
- Multimodal and multilingual NLP systems
- Reasoning, knowledge integration, and retrieval-augmented generation
- Ethics, fairness, bias mitigation, and safe deployment
- Interpretability and analysis of model behaviors
- Domain-specific applications in science, medicine, law, and more

## Who Should Attend

EMNLP 2026 is designed for a broad audience within the AI ecosystem. The primary attendees are academic and industrial research scientists and PhD students pushing the boundaries of NLP knowledge. It is equally critical for machine learning engineers and developers who implement state-of-the-art models in production environments and need to understand the practical implications of new research.

Furthermore, the conference is increasingly relevant for technical executives, product managers, and startup founders in the AI space who must make informed decisions about technology roadmaps. Professionals in adjacent fields like computational social science or digital humanities also find value in the methodologies and tools presented. In short, anyone whose work is fundamentally impacted by advances in language understanding and generation will find EMNLP 2026 to be a essential event.

## How to Register

Registration for EMNLP 2026 will be handled through the official conference website. Detailed pricing for early-bird, standard, student, and virtual attendance, as well as the exact opening date for registration, are to be announced by the organizing committee. Historically, registration opens several months before the conference. All interested parties are strongly advised to monitor the official EMNLP 2026 website for the most accurate and up-to-date information regarding registration, submission deadlines, and the final program schedule.
